newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BEARS WR CONWAY FRACTURES COLLARBONE, OUT 6-8 WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BEARS WR CONWAY FRACTURES COLLARBONE, OUT 6-8 WEEKS.

text.p: Curtis Conway, the first receiver in the history of the Chicago Bears to record back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons, fractured his left collarbone in Sunday night's preseason game against Arizona and will be sidelined six to eight weeks, the team announced.
Conway was injured when he dove for a pass in the second quarter and Cardinals rookie cornerback Ty Howard landed on top of him. He did not return to the game.

The 26-year-old Conway, who is entering the second year of a four-year, $10 million contract, finished the 1996 season with career-highs in receptions (81) and receiving yards (1,049). He emerged as one of the league's top receivers in 1995 when he caught 62 passes for 1,037 yards and 12 touchdowns.

A first-round pick and the seventh overall selection in the 1993 draft, Conway was used primarily as a kick returner in his rookie season. He averaged 21.4 yards on returns and had 19 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns.
Conway became more involved in the Bears' offense in his second year when he caught 39 passes for 546 yards and two touchdowns.
